name: A* Search
summary: Finds the shortest path to a goal and uses a guess of the remaining distance to search in the right direction first.
description: A* (say "A star") finds the shortest path from a start to a goal, for example for a character in a game or for a route on a map. Here the map is a grid with walls, and every step goes up, down, left or right. The code gets the grid as a graph in which graph[cell] lists the free neighbors of a cell, and h[cell], the Manhattan distance from the cell to the goal: the number of steps it would take if there were no walls.

For every cell it reaches, A* knows g, the number of steps from the start, and h, the estimate of the steps that are still left. It always explores the cell in the open list with the smallest f = g + h, so the path that looks most promising in total. Every neighbor that gets a smaller g remembers the cell it came from, its parent. Because h never overestimates the real distance, the goal is only picked once no shorter path can be left, and following the parents back to the start gives the shortest path.

Dijkstra's algorithm is A* with h = 0: it spreads out in every direction. Greedy best-first search only looks at h and rushes toward the goal, but its path can be longer. A* combines both. On a tie it takes the cell that was added last (the <= in the code), so it keeps following its newest path instead of spreading out.

This simple version scans the open list for the next cell, so it takes O(V²) time, where V is the number of free cells. In the best case nothing is in the way and A* walks straight along the d cells of the path. With a priority queue the next cell is found faster and A* runs in O(E log V).
